In Scimitar syndrome, this is classically caused by right lung hypoplasia or aplasia (often involving the right upper lobe or entire lung), leading to volume loss. Option B correctly identifies aplasia/hypoplasia as the cause of volume loss and dextroposition. Options A, C, D, E, and F describe mechanisms inconsistent with the classic presentation of Scimitar syndrome (which involves right-sided hypoplasia, not left collapse, effusion, mass, or bilateral disease)."}
